az_high_life_wall.blurb: High Life Wall is a bolted limestone face in Jacks Canyon, east of Flagstaff near Winslow. All 18 routes are sport climbs, and the wall leans toward the hard end: a handful of 5.8 lines to warm up on, then a cluster of 5.11 and 5.12 pitches that make up most of the tally. Lines run a bit longer than is typical elsewhere in the canyon. It lies at the far end of the developed cliffs, a short stroll beyond Cracker Jack Cliffs, which tends to keep the crowds thinner than at the main walls. Sun reaches it around midday, with shade in the early and late hours.

az_nose_rock.blurb: Nose Rock is the westernmost developed cliff at The Pit, the long-established sport crag just south of Flagstaff. Its 18 routes are all bolted and mostly short, climbing edges and pockets on good limestone. Difficulty skews toward the middle and upper grades: one route in the 5.9 range, a few 5.10s, then mostly 5.11 with a smaller group of 5.12 and 5.13 and a single 5.14. Not a spot for beginners, but a solid choice for intermediate to strong climbers wanting technical, powerful movement. Reaching it means a walk of roughly twenty minutes along the main trail, heading left past a big roof.

az_1_skeletor_area.blurb: Skeletor Area is the first cluster of boulders you meet on the trail up Middle Elden, on the slopes above Flagstaff. It holds 18 problems spanning V0 to V7, with the bulk in the V3 to V5 range, so there is something for people warming up and a few tougher lines for stronger climbers. Several problems are slabby or follow arete features. The boulders sit beside the path, making them quick to reach, and the spot tends to catch sun for much of the day. Bring pads, and expect a good place to loosen up before heading further up the canyon.

az_4_superfly_sector.blurb: Superfly Sector is a broad, open stretch of limestone wall in Dry Canyon, in the Whetstone Mountains of southern Arizona, lying between the Spine Cave and Bee Cave sectors. All 17 routes are sport, and this is serious terrain: most sit in the 5.13 range, with a few 5.10s, 5.11s and 5.12s to round things out. Several pitches are long enough that a 70 metre rope is wise. Reach the cliff by the single trail that makes one large switchback, then continue past Spine Cave. Better suited to experienced sport climbers than anyone new to the grade scale.

az_main_ampitheater.blurb: Main Amphitheater is the centrepiece of The Biscuit, a limestone cliff in the Mustang Mountains of southern Arizona, built around four large stacked roofs. It has 17 sport routes, most between 5.10 and 5.12 with a single 5.9, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate-to-hard bolted lines. The wall sits in shade in the morning, then turns hot and windless after the early afternoon, so mornings and the hour around dusk work best. Swifts nest here and fly out at evening. Watch for snakes tucked into holes at the base.

az_matterhorn_boulder.blurb: Matterhorn Boulder is a tall, ship-prow-shaped block perched on a small rise beside the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, near Tucson, in the Windy Ridge zone. It carries 17 problems on sharp but good granite, and the range is wide: several easy V1 lines and a V2 or V3 for newcomers, then a long run of V5 to V9 for strong climbers. Only a short walk from the road, it is easy to combine with other stops on the mountain, and Mount Lemmon's elevation keeps climbing possible through much of the year.

az_ridgeline.blurb: Ridgeline is a small sport crag in the mid-mountain zone of Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson. It has 17 bolted routes and is friendly to newer leaders: grades start near 5.5 and run up to 5.10, with the heaviest concentration in the 5.8 to 5.9 range. The base is shaded, which helps on warm days at this elevation. Getting there takes a short uphill walk and a brief descent to the cliff. Some climbs finish on a separate pinnacle and need a rappel back down, so bring your own rappel setup.
